question: According to the stoichiometry of complete biological nitrification (ammonia oxidized to nitrate), how many grams of O2 are required per gram of NH4-N oxidized, neglecting biomass synthesis? Provide the numeric value with units.
gold_explanation: Complete two-step nitrification (NH4+ -> NO2- -> NO3-) requires 4.57 g O2 per g NH4-N oxidized: 3.43 g O2/g N for ammonia oxidation (AOB) plus 1.14 g O2/g N for nitrite oxidation (NOB). This is the textbook stoichiometric oxygen demand assuming negligible cell synthesis. ASM1 uses (4.57 - Y_A)/Y_A in the autotrophic growth process, which collapses to 4.57 in the limit of zero yield.
citation: Henze et al. 2000, IWA STR No. 9, Ch. 3; Metcalf & Eddy 2014, Ch. 8 Sec. 8-3.

question: In the stoichiometry of heterotrophic denitrification of nitrate to N2 gas (ignoring cell synthesis), what is the oxygen-equivalent COD demand per gram of NO3-N reduced? Give the numeric factor with units.
gold_explanation: Reducing NO3- to N2 transfers 5 electrons per N atom. The corresponding oxygen-equivalent COD demand is 2.86 g COD per g NO3-N denitrified. This is the basis of the (1 - Y_H)/(2.86 Y_H) coefficient on NO3 in the ASM1 anoxic-growth process.
citation: Henze et al. 1987 IAWPRC STR No. 1; Henze et al. 2000 IWA STR No. 9.

question: What is the default heterotrophic biomass yield Y_H in ASM1 at 20 C, with units?
gold_explanation: The default ASM1 heterotrophic yield is Y_H = 0.67 g cell COD formed per g COD substrate utilized (aerobic and anoxic growth of heterotrophs use the same Y_H in the original ASM1).
citation: Henze et al. 1987 IAWPRC STR No. 1, Table 2; Henze et al. 2000 IWA STR No. 9, Tables 3.2-3.3.

question: What is the default autotrophic biomass yield Y_A in ASM1 at 20 C, with units?
gold_explanation: The default ASM1 autotrophic yield is Y_A = 0.24 g cell COD formed per g N oxidized (NH4-N oxidized to NO3-N). Together with the 4.57 g O2/g N total electron demand, this gives the ASM1 oxygen sink coefficient (4.57 - Y_A)/Y_A on the autotrophic growth process.
citation: Henze et al. 1987 IAWPRC STR No. 1, Table 2; Henze et al. 2000 IWA STR No. 9, Tables 3.2-3.3.

question: Per gram of NH4-N nitrified, how many grams of alkalinity (expressed as CaCO3) are consumed? Provide the numeric value with units.
gold_explanation: Nitrification releases 2 mol H+ per mol NH4+ oxidized to NO3-. Expressed as CaCO3 equivalent alkalinity, this corresponds to 7.14 g CaCO3 destroyed per g NH4-N nitrified (= 2 x 50 / 14). Inadequate alkalinity collapses pH and stalls nitrification.
citation: Metcalf & Eddy 2014, Ch. 8 Sec. 8-3; U.S. EPA 1993 Process Design Manual for Nitrogen Control.

question: Under anoxic conditions in an activated-sludge system, which oxidized nitrogen species do heterotrophic bacteria use as a terminal electron acceptor in place of oxygen, and what is the gaseous end-product when denitrification proceeds to completion?
gold_explanation: In anoxic zones, heterotrophs use nitrate (NO3-) as the terminal electron acceptor; the oxidized N is reduced through the sequence NO3- -> NO2- -> NO -> N2O -> N2, with dinitrogen gas (N2) as the complete denitrification end-product.
citation: Henze et al. 2000 IWA STR No. 9, Ch. 3; Metcalf & Eddy 2014, Ch. 8 Sec. 8-4; Grady et al. 2011 Biological Wastewater Treatment, Ch. 2.

question: Under fully aerobic conditions in a nitrifying activated-sludge reactor at low to moderate DO, what is the dominant biological pathway by which N2O is produced, and which functional group of organisms is responsible?
gold_explanation: Under aerobic, nitrifying conditions - especially at low DO and/or with elevated nitrite - the dominant N2O production pathway is nitrifier denitrification carried out by ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB), which reduce NO2- to NO and then to N2O.
forbidden: heterotrophic denitrification is the dominant aerobic
citation: Kampschreur et al. 2009 Water Research 43:4093; Wunderlin et al. 2012 Water Research 46:1027.

question: In Enhanced Biological Phosphorus Removal (EBPR), what do polyphosphate-accumulating organisms (PAOs) do during the ANAEROBIC phase: which substrate do they take up, what intracellular polymer do they store, and what is released to the bulk liquid as the energy source for that uptake?
gold_explanation: In the anaerobic phase of EBPR, PAOs take up volatile fatty acids (VFAs, principally acetate) from the bulk liquid and store them intracellularly as polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA, primarily PHB). The energy for VFA uptake comes from hydrolysis of intracellular polyphosphate, which releases orthophosphate (PO4) to the bulk liquid.
forbidden: nitrate is the electron acceptor anaerobically
citation: Henze et al. 2000 IWA STR No. 9, Ch. 4-5; Metcalf & Eddy 2014, Ch. 8 Sec. 8-7; Mino, van Loosdrecht & Heijnen 1998 Water Research 32:3193.

question: For reliable, year-round nitrification in a conventional activated-sludge system designed for a winter mixed-liquor temperature of about 10 C, what is the typical recommended minimum aerobic SRT (solids retention time)?
gold_explanation: Standard textbook design practice gives a minimum aerobic SRT of approximately 10-15 days at 10 C (with values around 8-10 d at 12-15 C and ~4-5 d at 20 C).
citation: Metcalf & Eddy 2014 5th ed., Ch. 8 Sec. 8-3 Table 8-14; Grady et al. 2011, Ch. 11.

question: What is the typical minimum bulk-liquid dissolved-oxygen concentration recommended in conventional activated-sludge design textbooks for reliable nitrification (i.e., to avoid floc-diffusion limitation of AOB)?
gold_explanation: Standard activated-sludge design practice recommends maintaining bulk DO of approximately 2.0 mg/L (typical range 1.5-2.0 mg/L) in nitrifying aerobic zones to overcome diffusion limitation in flocs.
citation: Metcalf & Eddy 2014 5th ed., Ch. 8 Sec. 8-3 and Ch. 5; WEF MOP 8 (2018) Vol. 2.

question: How is the F/M (food-to-microorganism) ratio in an activated-sludge system defined, and what is the typical range for conventional plug-flow / complete-mix activated sludge operating in BOD-removal mode?
gold_explanation: F/M = (influent flow x influent BOD5) / (aeration tank volume x MLVSS), i.e. mass of BOD5 applied per day per mass of MLVSS in the aeration basin (units: kg BOD5 / (kg MLVSS . d) or 1/d). For conventional activated sludge the typical operating range is 0.2-0.5 kg BOD5 / (kg MLVSS . d).
forbidden: f/m is mlss divided by bod
citation: Metcalf & Eddy 2014 5th ed., Ch. 8 Sec. 8-2 Table 8-2; Tchobanoglous et al. 2003 4th ed., Ch. 8.

question: Holding all else constant, what is the directional effect of decreasing mixed-liquor temperature from 20 C to 10 C on the maximum specific growth rate of autotrophic nitrifiers, and is the effect larger or smaller than for heterotrophs? Answer with the direction and the relative magnitude.
gold_explanation: The maximum specific growth rate of autotrophic nitrifiers DECREASES with decreasing temperature, and the effect is LARGER for autotrophs than for heterotrophs. ASM1 default temperature coefficients give mu_A roughly halving from 20 C to 10 C (theta ~1.10-1.12 for autotrophs vs. theta ~1.04-1.07 for heterotrophs).
forbidden: heterotrophs more temperature sensitive than nitrifiers
citation: Henze et al. 2000 IWA STR No. 9, Ch. 3 Table 3.3; Metcalf & Eddy 2014, Ch. 8 Sec. 8-3 Eq. 8-26-8-28.
